subject: Computer Networking
title: Inside Email Headers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Inside Email Headers.

hook.text: Every email has hidden metadata. Headers record the full journey, from origin to your inbox.

buildup.text: Headers include From, To, Subject, Date, and a unique Message-ID assigned by the sender's server.

discovery.text: Received headers are added at each hop. The bottom one is the origin, the top is the final server.

twist.text: Spammers forge From headers easily. Authentication headers like SPF and DKIM reveal the truth.

climax.text: Reply chains use In-Reply-To and References headers to thread messages. Your client reads these.

punchline.text: Headers are email's audit trail. Every hop leaves a stamp.

quiz.question: What do 'Received' headers in an email show?
options: Each server the email passed through on its journey
The number of times the email was opened
The attachments included in the email

details.summary: Email headers contain metadata about the message including sender, recipient, date, subject, and a record of every server the email passed through. The Received headers create a trace route showing the email's journey. Headers are essential for debugging delivery problems and detecting spoofing.
details.whyItMatters: Email headers are the forensic evidence of delivery. They reveal where an email really came from, what path it took, and whether authentication checks passed or failed.
takeaways: Headers record every server the email passed through
Received headers create a trace route of the delivery path
Authentication results from SPF, DKIM, and DMARC appear in headers

faq.question: How do you read email headers to trace a message?
faq.answer: Received headers are added by each server in reverse order. Read from bottom to top to follow the chronological path. Each Received line shows the server name, IP address, and timestamp. Comparing timestamps reveals where delays occurred in the delivery chain.

faq.question: Can email headers be forged?
faq.answer: The From header is trivially forgeable. However, Received headers added by each server are more reliable. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication results in headers reveal whether the sender is legitimate. Modern email clients use these authentication results to flag suspicious messages.
